neighbours.label: a noun for an interconnected set of things, before ' of' ('a network of', 'a web of', 'a chain of', 'a system of')
fire: The empire was held together by a vast network of paved roads.
The fraud involved a tangled web of shell companies.
A long chain of events led to the closing of the mine.
The old city is cut through by a dense grid of narrow streets.
Beneath the forest lies a fine mesh of fungal threads.
The farmers built a system of canals to water the fields.
The hospital is linked to a network of rural clinics.
Visitors get lost in the maze of tunnels under the castle.
quiet: The empire was held together by a large army of paid soldiers.
The fraud involved a huge sum of stolen money.
A long period of drought led to the closing of the mine.
The old city is cut through by a wide river with muddy banks.
Beneath the forest lies a thick layer of wet clay.
The farmers built a pair of barns to store the grain.
The hospital is next to a row of small houses.
Visitors get lost in the crowd of tourists near the castle.

notes: Card: ' network' x7, ' web' x2, ' system' x2, ' chain' x2, ' cycle' x2, ' pattern', ' line of'. Probe: 'complex web of' 0.632; 'network of' 0.389, 0.349; 'chain of' 0.343; 'lattice of' 0.201; 'pile of' 0.066. New cases in the test: mesh, grid, tangle, maze.
